the reference's embedded chroma XML lexers. Recover them with devutils/embedextract: `go build -o /tmp/embedextract ./devutils/embedextract` then `/tmp/embedextract -bin ~/.local/bin/agy -embed-out <dir>` writes the //go:embed file systems; the 279 files under its 'embedded/' root are upstream chroma's lexers/embedded/*.xml, and the 74 at the root are upstream's styles/*.xml. Each line here is '<file base> <the alias that lexer registers>'. At 1.4.8 all 353 embedded files are still byte-identical to upstream chroma v2.27.0, so a changed file set at a new release means the reference's chroma moved and the clone's dependency pin must follow it - see docs/cycles/cycle-300-chroma-parity/deliverable.md

run the real agy with CLOUD_CODE_URL pointed at devutils/refcapture, a mock that forwards every RPC except streamGenerateContent to the real CloudCode endpoint, answers the agent turn with one functionCall, and then reads functionResponse.response.output in the follow-up request the reference sends. the reference's own per-tool descriptions, read out of agy (~/.local/bin/agy, sha256 09fcdd8554e03bed9b2ec936e454c7f115d5610610de09ed7d79fa2feae76940). The binary has three tool surfaces: the advertised list (names only), the converter layer (cortex/tools/*, gemini_coder/framework/toolconverters - the prose that assembles a tool definition) and the runtime layer (cortex/core/tools/tools, oneharness/internal/tools/tools - the Description() methods, twelve of which are the declarations the reference sends to the model). Thirty-seven of the sixty-three advertised names carry text - the thirty-seventh is browser_subagent, whose text lives in the binary's built-in agents package (cortex/customizations/builtin/agents) rather than in a tool layer; 'layer' records which surface each text came from, 'complete' is false for run_workflow (fragments only). run_command's 'text' is the reference's converter template with the operating system, the shell and the two prose parts substituted - the darwin rendering - and its 'model_facing' field holds the runtime text the reference's declaration carries. Every literal (or its fragment) is still present in the 1.4.8 binary, byte for byte. Re-verify by reading the literals out of the binary at the addresses the report gives

the reference's second set of model-facing tool texts. agy 1.4.8 holds two variants of four descriptions (run_command, send_message, manage_subagents, edit_file); the default - the one a live session sends - is what internal/tools/model_tools_1.4.6.json carries, and the alternates are recorded here with the vmaddr/length of every literal they are built from.
